projects.title: Video Game Organizer/Database
projects.description:
A full-stack game library manager I built to solve a problem I actually had: no easy way to catalog a physical game collection or track what's worth buying. Users can snap a photo of their shelf, and the app runs OCR combined with LLM parsing (OpenAI) to automatically extract and clean up game titles, no manual entry required. It also syncs directly with Steam via OAuth to pull in a user's full owned-game library.

Each game page aggregates data from three separate APIs (RAWG, IsThereAnyDeal, and Steam) into one unified view, covering details, pricing, deals, and storefront links. Users can organize their library into custom collections through a Firestore-backed grouping system, beyond default status categories.

Built with React on the front end, Firebase for auth, storage, and database, and a Node.js/Express backend handling the OCR and API calls.

projects.title: Soylent Eccomerce
projects.description:
A pixel-perfect clone of Soylant's ecommerce site, built to practice replicating a real production-level design and building out full ecommerce functionality behind it. The app supports three purchase types per product (subscribe, one-time, and prepaid), each with its own pricing and quantity logic, mirroring how real subscription-commerce sites work.

Checkout runs through a custom Express backend that creates a real Stripe Checkout session and handles secure payment redirection. The cart persists across page reloads using localStorage, and automatically filters out items a user already owns when suggesting related products.

Originally built in JavaScript, I later migrated the entire app to TypeScript, adding typed data models and type-safe event handling throughout to make the codebase more maintainable and catch errors earlier.

Built with React and TypeScript on the front end, Stripe for payments, and a Node.js/Express backend.
